summary: Confirmed DONE. In standard and desktop builds, the static boot graph from main.tsx carries no hosted relay, E2EE, noble, cborg or Hub-API code, and neither do the RootAppShell and ChatThreadRouteView closures. The build-time seam plugin swaps hostedHub/state, transport, bootGate, the coordinator, HostedConnectionControls, NoActiveThreadHostedStatus and pwa/lifecycle for inert *.standard siblings. The relay barrel no longer re-exports the E2EE initiator or channel. In hosted builds, the initiator and noble load through import("./e2eeRuntime"), which starts when the account authenticates and is awaited before a ticket is bought. If the code is not loaded yet, the attempt fails closed. I checked this in two ways: (a) an independent source-graph walk with the seams applied (standard main.tsx: 388 modules, none heavy and hosted; hosted main.tsx: no @noble), and (b) the current apps/web/dist, which contains HEAD-only code (worktree-setup-spin), so it was built from HEAD. In that dist the relay engine, the E2EE handshake and cborg appear in no chunk, and the authorization/api code appears only in api-*.js, which the boot and shell chunks do not import statically. The auditor made two mistakes. First, regression guards do exist. Second, it understated one leftover: the settings route is idle-preloaded on every standard launch and pulls in the Hub API chunk.

evidence.note: Seam list. The plugin at :56-91 is registered first at apps/web/vite.config.ts:104. It applies only to non-test standard builds (shouldApplyClientModeSeams), which is the build desktop ships (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:2123 loads apps/web/dist).

Imports the authorization barrel for types only. Its values come from the light authorization/hostedStores subpath, so the real state.ts and its static ./runtime -> ./e2eeAttempt chain are hosted-only.
The E2EE initiator and channel are no longer re-exported; at f1be4abc7 the barrel exported both. They live only at the ./relay/e2ee subpath (packages/client-runtime/src/relay/e2ee.ts).

loadWebRelayE2ee does import("./e2eeRuntime") and retries after a failed load. prepareWebRelayE2ee (:146) is the runtime's prepareRelaySocketContext, which transport.ts:224 awaits before buying a ticket. resolveWebRelayE2eeProvider (:313) fails closed (retryable close, never plaintext) if the code is not loaded. scheduleWebE2eeWarmUp (:430) starts the load when the account authenticates.

Source-level regression guard the auditor missed. With the seams applied, it walks main.tsx and RootAppShell.tsx (also PullRequestsPage) and forbids @noble, cborg, shared relayE2ee*/relayCodec, the relay engine, the heavy authorization modules and the real seam modules.

Dist-level guard the auditor missed. HOSTED_RUNTIME_SOURCES are forbidden in the boot, RootAppShell, ChatThreadRouteView and PullRequestsRouteView closures of the real build. CI runs it after every web build (.github/workflows/_validation.yml:208-213, `bun run perf:bundle-budget`, with hidden sourcemaps). There is no SettingsRouteView closure.

evidence.location: apps/web/dist/assets (built 2026-10-14 21:45, after HEAD commit at 21:40, contains HEAD-only class worktree-setup-spin)
evidence.note: The static closure of index-* is boot-* + boot-vendor-* + main-* (1.60 MB raw). These strings appear in no dist chunk: relayEngine ('RPC payload exceeds the maximum relay message size.'), the Noise handshake, the relayE2eeInitiator strings, cborg ('CBOR decode error'), and hostedConnectionCoordinator. authorization/api.ts appears only in api-BJhIvEex.js and authorization/state.ts only in AccountSettings-* and HostedHubRoot-*. The RootAppShell, ChatThreadRouteView, DraftChatThreadRouteView and CommandPaletteDialog closures are clean.

Leftover, not on the boot path. SettingsPanels.tsx:547 renders DeviceIdentitySettings in standard builds, and it statically imports hostedHubApi, which is used only in the isHostedHubMode() branch at :36-38. In dist, SettingsRouteView -> SettingsPage -> SettingsPanels -> api-BJhIvEex.js (66.4 KB raw / 17.9 KB gzip: HostedHubApi, hosted contracts schemas, webauthn and passkey).

ShellIdlePreloads calls preloadSettingsPage (settingsRoute.ts:21-29) on every non-phone launch after the shell paints, unless data saver or a slow network is on. So the api chunk above is downloaded and evaluated in essentially every standard/desktop session, though only in idle time.

Negligible hosted-only leftover. It imports one constant from @ryco/shared/relayE2eeWire, which keeps that module and its top-level cborg encode (relayE2eeWire.ts:535) on the hosted boot path. cborg itself is needed there anyway by relayCodec (relay engine), so the extra cost is only relayE2eeWire's own few KiB.

fixDefects: The fix itself has no defect. It does miss one shared-code caller: apps/web/src/components/settings/DeviceIdentitySettings.tsx:6 statically imports hostedHubApi from hostedHub/api, which is not a seam. SettingsPanels renders this component in standard builds. As a result, the standard settings route closure contains api-*.js (66.4 KB raw / 17.9 KB gzip of HostedHubApi, hosted schemas and webauthn). RootAppShell idle-preloads that route on every standard/desktop launch (RootAppShell.tsx:184), so the hosted Hub API client is still fetched and evaluated in nearly every standard session, after first paint. It is not on the boot path and contains no relay, E2EE or noble code. The bundle-budget policy does not catch it because it has no SettingsRouteView closure.
implementationSketch: 1. DeviceIdentitySettings.tsx: drop the static `import { hostedHubApi } from "../../hostedHub/api"`. In the `isHostedHubMode() && hostedNode` branch of `rename`, use `const { hostedHubApi } = await import("../../hostedHub/api");`. isHostedHubMode() reads the build-time define, so standard builds drop the import. HostedNodeRenameDialog can stay or be lazy-mounted. (An alternative is to add hostedHub/api.ts to CLIENT_MODE_SEAM_MODULES with an api.standard.ts that throws HostedOnlyEntryPointError, but AccountSettings, HostedHubRoot and NativeAuthorization would all need it, so the local dynamic import is simpler.) 2. scripts/perf/model.ts DEFAULT_BUNDLE_BUDGET_POLICY: add a { name: "SettingsRouteView", chunk: "SettingsRouteView", beyondBoot: true, maxGzipBytes: null, forbiddenSources: HOSTED_RUNTIME_SOURCES } closure. Its authorization/(?!light) rule already matches authorization/api.ts, so it fails today and passes after step 1. 3. apps/web/src/perf/standardBootGraph.test.ts: add forbiddenChains("components/settings/SettingsPanels.tsx", [...HOSTED_RUNTIME, /^apps\/web\/src\/hostedHub\/api\.ts$/u]). 4. Verify with `bun run --cwd apps/web test src/perf/standardBootGraph.test.ts src/components/settings` and a hosted-mode browser test of the node rename flow.
decisionReason: No E2EE, auth or Hub protocol semantics change. The leftover fix only changes how a hosted-only call site loads the Hub API client.
correction: The auditor's fixDefects (2) is wrong. Regression guards cover the standard build's module graph and output: apps/web/src/perf/standardBootGraph.test.ts (source graph with seams applied, main.tsx and RootAppShell, forbidding noble, cborg, relay, authorization and the real seam modules) and the CI bundle-budget check scripts/perf/model.ts:214-298, run in .github/workflows/_validation.yml:208-213 on the real dist. The auditor's leftover (1) is real but understated. The settings chunks are not only lazy: RootAppShell.tsx:184 idle-preloads the settings route on every standard launch, so api-*.js (66.4 KB raw / 17.9 KB gzip) is fetched and evaluated in nearly every session. The auditor's claim that the 66 KB api chunk is 'only listed in RootAppShell's __vite__mapDeps preload list' is also imprecise. That list is for the PhoneSettingsSurface import, while the chunk that matters statically imports it: SettingsPanels-*.js, reached from SettingsRouteView.
